![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14227445/assets/48d9d8513f45b87f9deffeffcef31e49a6dcaba0b033c91a918c1d72d87eb215.png)

In the quadrilateral $ABCD$ above, determine the measure of $∠C.$
question.worked_solution:
A quadrilateral has $n=4$ sides. Therefore, the sum of the interior angles of a quadrilateral  must be 

$$
\begin{aligned}{180}^{∘}\cdot (n-2) & ={180}^{∘}\cdot (4-2) \\  & ={180}^{∘}\cdot 2 \\  & ={360}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Adding up the internal angles and solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠A+m∠B+m∠C+m∠D & ={360}^{∘} \\ x+{90}^{∘}+3x+6x & ={360}^{∘} \\ 10x+{90}^{∘} & ={360}^{∘} \\ 10x & ={270}^{∘} \\ x & ={27}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠C & =3x \\  & =3({27}^{∘}) \\  & ={81}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$
